networkHosts.artifact: Node headers and libs for a from-source native compile
fetchedBy: node-gyp (any native-build package, including an implicit `node-gyp rebuild` for a root binding.gyp)
networkHosts.observed: node-gyp's default dist URL, reached whenever the header cache is cold. NOT observed in the 311-package corpus run: that harness sets `npm_config_nodedir` to the provisioned Node root, as nub does, so node-gyp never fetched. Absence there is not evidence the entry is unnecessary — it is evidence the corpus did not exercise a cold header cache.

Named in Prisma's own firewall-allowlist documentation. A grep of the fetched postinstall bundle found no literal match, so the constant lives in a helper chunk that pass did not fetch. Not independently confirmed from source.
Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run. Paired with cdn.cypress.io because the 302 lands there; granting only one leaves the install broken.

Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run, as the redirect target of download.cypress.io. cypress is the one corpus package that installs successfully under this four-host list.

packageGrants.mechanism: scripts/postinstall.js does three things, and each masks the next: it calls process.chdir(INIT_CWD); createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles unconditionally mkdirs path.join(__dirname, '../../../.prisma'), a sibling of @prisma in the package's own enclosing node_modules; then it re-execs the prisma CLI as `prisma generate`, which reads the consumer's prisma/ schema directory. The generated client lands inside package_dir and needs no grant.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/.prisma, then EPERM uv_cwd on chdir(INIT_CWD), then EPERM reading the consumer's prisma/ schema. Verified by artifact, not exit code: a generated client of 71282 B carrying a per-run schema nonce, against absent output and 2 EPERMs without the grants. Presence alone is not a valid check here — the script writes throw-stubs before every guard, so it exits 0 having generated nothing.

packageGrants.mechanism: Its postinstall runs `indefinitely-typed`, which computes path.resolve(cwd, '../..'), asserts that directory is named node_modules, then mkdirs @types there and copySyncs each --folder argument into it. The write target is <own node_modules>/@types — the same enclosing-node_modules sibling shape as Prisma, under a different name.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/@types. With the grant, 20 copied type folders present; without it, absent.

packageGrants.mechanism: config/scripts/postinstall.js reads the CONSUMER's package.json for msw.workerDirectory, returns silently if absent, and otherwise re-execs its own CLI with cwd set to INIT_CWD to copy mockServiceWorker.js into each listed directory. The directories come from the field rather than a literal because msw imposes no convention — the consumer picks them.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM uv_cwd. The cwd need bites first: without projectCwd the child dies in uv_cwd before it reads the field at all. With the grants, msw's worker script is present; without them, absent.

notGranted.comment: Documentation only. Nothing in this object is compiled into any allowlist; it records hosts that a real install was measured to need and that were nonetheless refused, so a contributor can see the bar before opening a PR. A test asserts this list and networkHosts stay disjoint.

hosts.detail: 46 corpus packages fetch release tarballs here (14 blocking), so the demand is real and measured. Refused anyway: an unauthenticated write probe returns path-varying statuses, meaning routes that accept a write exist under the same hostname. Host-level DNS gating cannot restrict this to /releases/download/. Needs pre-download brokering, not an allowlist entry.

Needed by puppeteer, taiko, chromedriver and @tensorflow/tfjs-node for Chrome and libtensorflow artifacts. Refused because an attacker can rent a bucket under the same hostname and read back whatever a confined script writes there — the exfiltration criterion, not an integrity one.

@aws-amplify/cli fetches its binary here and reports `failed to install amplify binary` when egress is denied, but the install itself still succeeds (rc 0). A soft fetch that degrades rather than failing does not earn an entry.
